From athletics to weightlifting, find out how gymnastics has helped our homegrown heroes to thrive!",{"id":925,"contentType":560,"image":926},"69cecc7f-e312-401a-9bb8-cb5f0e8a8498","https://media-cdn.cortextech.io/MH8SRGat/1BSdBWIjChWbTd/270c3a99-2687-41fe-9450-e1748310dbc8.png",5,[929,931],{"sourceSystem":566,"sourceSystemId":930},"270c3a99-2687-41fe-9450-e1748310dbc8",{"sourceSystem":566,"sourceSystemId":932},"997c174f-a3a9-4912-8ad5-09d929176ca2",[934],{"id":854,"text":172},{"id":854,"text":172},{"sourceSystem":937},"CORTEX",{},[940,943,946,950,953,956,959,962,965],{"id":941,"contentType":579,"content":942,"isHtml":13},"ce6ae5ca-7ba1-453b-bef9-05986e83518b","What do Australia’s fastest woman and the reigning high jump World Champion have in common? They have both benefited from having a go at gymnastics! \n\nGymnastics has a range of physical and cognitive benefits, developing coordination, strength, flexibility, balance, self-confidence and more. These fundamental skills provide a strong foundation that empowers gymnasts to succeed not only across a range of sports, but in all aspects of life.\n\nAs the Commonwealth Games wrap up in Glasgow, here’s a look at three 2026 Commonwealth Games superstars who have benefited from their time at a Gymnastics NSW affiliated club!",{"id":944,"contentType":579,"content":945,"isHtml":13},"bd7619c6-8713-4d5b-aa5b-e41084fa2d16","#### **Torrie Lewis - Sprinter**\n\n2024 Paris Olympian and 2026 Commonwealth Games Bronze Medallist **Torrie Lewis** was six years old when she started classes at Blackert Gymnastics Academy in the Hunter region. \n\nTraining Women’s Artistic Gymnastics, Lewis worked her way through the levels system before deciding to focus her attention on athletics. \n\nAt the 2026 Commonwealth Games, Lewis became [the first Australian woman to break the 11-second barrier in the 100m sprint](https://commonwealthgames.com.au/patterson-completes-glasgow-fairytale-as-sprinters-fire-and-robinson-wins-gold/), winning bronze in the 100m final with a time of 10.99 seconds. Lewis also placed fourth in the 4x100m relay alongside Aussie teammates **Ebony Lane, Chloe Mannix** and **Monique Hanlon**, and finished sixth in her pet event, the 200m sprint.\n\nWhile the 21-year-old is making headlines for her incredible athletics achievements, she still fondly remembers her time at her local gymnastics club. \n\n“Wouldn’t be where I am today without my days at gym,” she said on social media.",{"id":947,"contentType":560,"content":948,"image":949},"82a2903c-aeaf-4e9a-8461-bbeb8c55c192","Torrie Lewis competes on beam at the 2012 Gymnastics NSW State Championships.","https://media-cdn.cortextech.io/MH8SRGat/1BSdBWIjChWbTd/997c174f-a3a9-4912-8ad5-09d929176ca2.jpg",{"id":951,"contentType":579,"content":952,"isHtml":13},"83a296a5-6a03-4c63-b83b-4a8b6e915feb","#### **Kiana Elliott - Weightlifter**\n\nTokyo 2020 Olympian and two-time Commonwealth Games representative **Kiana Elliott** also started her sporting journey as a gymnast. \n\nAfter attending a gymnastics session at her primary school, Elliott was encouraged to start training at her local club. Noted for her skill and work ethic, Elliott trained alongside 2024 Paris Olympian **Emma Nedov** at the Y Epping and was a member of the International Development Program. \n\nElliott stepped away from gymnastics at age 14 and later took up CrossFit for fun and fitness. Already lifting weights that would challenge state records, she was connected with a local weightlifting coach and went on to place seventh at the Youth Olympic Games in Nanjing, China just over a year later.\n\nAt her first Commonwealth Games in 2022, Elliott placed fourth in the 71kg weight division. Competing in the 63kg weight division in Glasgow, Elliott once again finished agonisingly short of the podium, finishing in fourth place by just two kilograms. \n\nOne of Australia’s leading weightlifters, Elliott’s time as a gymnast has helped shape both the athlete and person she is today. \n\n“My sporting background has definitely given me a huge leg up in weightlifting not only physically, but also in teaching the skills and attitudes of an athlete,” Elliott wrote on her social media.  \n\n“I can truly say I wouldn't be the person I am today without the gymnastics background.”",{"id":954,"contentType":579,"content":955,"isHtml":180},"26942053-412e-4ff5-a571-06ec82c5158e","\u003Cblockquote class=\"instagram-media\" data-instgrm-captioned Olympic silver medallist and 2025 World Champion **Nicola Olyslagers** was already one of the world’s best high jumpers when she began looking for a new competitive edge. \n\nAfter finishing third at the 2023 World Championships, Olyslagers and her strength and conditioning coach **Nicolai Morris** decided to try incorporating gymnastics into her training program to improve her strength, confidence and aerial awareness. \n\nThe results were immediate, providing both physical and mental benefits. \n\n“As a 27-year-old, it’s like I am in kindergarten again. It’s like bringing that childlike fun into the sport again,” she told the *Sydney Morning Herald* in 2024. \n\nTraining at United Gymnastics Academy on the Central Coast, Olyslagers found that practicing landing on different surfaces helped her adapt to varying track conditions while activities such as handstands and rope work offered a fresh challenge for upper-body strength and mobility. \n\nEven learning a back somersault helped boost her performance, improving her proprioception and body positioning, allowing her to clear the bar more consistently. \n\nIn August 2025, Olyslagers became [the first Australian woman to clear the elusive two-metre barrier](https://www.athletics.com.au/news/2-04m-and-rising-olyslagers-poised-for-world-title/) with a personal best jump of 2.04m. toes. After everything she had endured, simply returning to elite international competition was an achievement in itself. \n\n\"I'm really glad at the age of 28 I'm still able to do this sport that I love,” she said. “I've learnt to cherish each moment and every opportunity I get to wear the green and gold.\"  \n\nHer performances across the Games demonstrated both resilience and class. Olympic Park from 28 June to 20 July 2026, the stands were awash with a sea of blue as friends, family and supporters turned out in force to cheer on Team GNSW, creating an unforgettable atmosphere for the competitors.\n\nThe results speak for themselves with New South Wales topping the medal tally once again, recording our best ever total of 371 medals including 140 gold, 128 silver and 103 departing for Glasgow. \n\nNew South Wales' dominance in Men's Artistic Gymnastics continued as our Senior International and Level 9 Under teams claimed their fifth consecutive national titles while in Women's Artistic, a packed arena welcomed the return of fan favourites **Georgia Godwin** and **Larrissa Haven** to the national stage.\n\n2026 also marked the introduction of the Mixed Team Competition, a innovative new competition format which is set to appear at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics. The New South Wales team excelled across all four Trampoline disciplines, claiming five of the six available International Team titles. **Alexsa Kachan, Brock Batty, Eleni Fountis, Ethan McGuinness, Kyle Brett** and **Lauren Barter** also combined forces to secure the coveted Team All-Around title for another year, reinforcing the depth and quality of our state's programs and pathways.\n\nIn the final week of competition, it was the turn of our Acrobatic, Aerobic and Rhythmic gymnasts to take to the floor. New South Wales continued to dominate with our gymnasts sweeping multiple divisions in the Aerobic and Acrobatic competition, while our Rhythmic gymnasts also performed strongly.\n\n**Gymnastics NSW CEO Rebecca Shaw** praised the team for their performance and conduct throughout the Championships.\n\n“Seeing our gymnasts compete at the Australian Gymnastics Championships is a joy and having the event right here in our backyard makes it that much more special,\" she said. \n\n\"I would like to congratulate all the New South Wales gymnasts on their excellent performances and the way they have represented their state both on and off the competition floor. I would also like to acknowledge the coaches, family and friends who have supported them along the way and extend our gratitude to all the judges, officials, volunteers and staff whose commitment and Identical twins **Chloe** and **Willow Lai** have done just that. \n\nAfter representing Australia at the 2025 Rhythmic Gymnastics Junior World Championships, Chloe and Willow made the switch to aerobic gymnastics and are continuing to reach new heights. Now preparing for their fifth Australian Gymnastics Championships, and first in aerobics, we spoke to Chloe and Willow about their journey so far and the experiences that have shaped them along the way. \n\nChloe and Willow started gymnastics when they were four and a half years old. After trying both artistic and acrobatic gymnastics, the twins attended a Talent Identification Day at Le Ray Gymnastics, sparking an eight-year journey in rhythmic gymnastics. \n\n“My favourite thing about rhythmic gymnastics was learning new skills, working with the different apparatus and performing at competitions,” Willow told Gymnastics NSW. “I also really enjoyed training with the friends I made through the sport, which made all the hard work and long training sessions a lot more enjoyable.”",{"id":1221,"contentType":560,"content":1222,"image":1223},"cafb33c9-ecba-4f87-b84d-ae7c7663bc7e","Chloe and Willow (left) with their Development Group in and competing side by side, Chloe and Willow attended their first Australian Gymnastics Championships in 2021, competing in the Sub Junior division. \n\n“We were definitely nervous, but mostly excited to finally compete at a Nationals after all the hard work and training we'd done,” Chloe and Willow told Gymnastics NSW.  \n\n“One of our favourite parts was being able to watch some of Australia's top gymnasts and experience the atmosphere of such a big competition.” \n\nAfter years of dedication, in 2024 Chloe and Willow were both selected as members of the Le Ray Gymnastics Junior Group alongside **Anna Barsukova, Claire Chavdarova, Joselyn Cheung,** and **Victoria Wei**.  \n\nWhat followed was a whirlwind adventure, with the team making their international debut at the Aphrodite Cup in March 2025 before taking the floor at the [Junior World Championships](https://[hostname-redacted]/content/nsw-gymnasts-shine-at-international-events) just three months later. \n\nFor Willow, the opportunity to compete against the world’s best gymnasts and watch them perform is something she will never forget. \n\n“Being able to compete on such a big stage with my teammates was really special. Even though we'd only been together as a group for a short time, we achieved so much and made some great memories along the way,” she said.",{"id":1228,"contentType":560,"content":1229,"image":1230},"1a6bf3e8-bc20-4c4f-b0fe-a1ebf19d35d2","The Le Ray Gymnastics Junior Group at the 2025 Rhythmic Gymnastics Junior World Championships in Sofia, Bulgaria. ","https://media-cdn.cortextech.io/MH8SRGat/1BSdBWIjChWbLO/33c45d90-a396-4d00-a76c-0839552aa6ad.jpg",{"id":1232,"contentType":579,"content":1233,"isHtml":13},"fdd465f5-8c6b-45f6-b871-beb5185308f1","After close to a decade in rhythmic gymnastics and reaching one of the sport’s highest levels, the twins found themselves looking for their next challenge. \n\n“One of my friends who was already doing aerobics kept telling me how much fun it was, and the more I watched it, the more interested I became,” said Chloe.",{"id":1235,"text":1236,"contentType":1018,"title":1237},"bb1351e3-4d3a-4107-8779-2b3fb26583cc","“I loved how energetic and fast-paced it looked, and I was excited to see how some of the skills I'd developed in rhythmic gymnastics could carry across while learning a whole new discipline.”  ","Chloe Lai",{"id":1239,"contentType":579,"content":1240,"isHtml":13},"8be8a697-8ea3-41e8-8e51-302911159b9c","Deciding to take the leap, Chloe and Willow joined the aerobic gymnastics program at PLC Sydney. Their strong work ethic and years of elite-level training enabled them to make a quick transition to the new gymsport and at the beginning of 2026, both Chloe and Willow were selected for the NSW Junior Aerodance team.  \n\nThe team went on to win gold at their first international event, the [2026 Cantanhede Open](https://[hostname-redacted]/content/international-success-for-nsw-gymnasts) in March. \n\n“It was my first time visiting Portugal, which made the trip even more memorable,” said Chloe. \n\n“We performed early in the competition, so we then had to wait and watch the other groups before the results were announced. The wait felt like forever, but when we found out we'd won first place, we couldn't believe it. It was such a special moment and definitely one of my favourite memories so far.”",{"id":1242,"contentType":560,"content":1243,"image":1244},"1a968950-b248-495e-9027-83944449f89b","The Junior Aerodance Team competes at the 2026 Cantanhede Open. Team, One Dream: The KSTP story","Founded in 2009 by Dima and Rebecca Kachan, the Kachan School of Tumbling and Performance has produced over 100 individual National Champions and played a vital role in the resurgence of tumbling in Australia.",{"id":1261,"contentType":560,"image":1262},"11577bf5-10f8-4a40-b2b3-931c3e0af69a","https://media-cdn.cortextech.io/MH8SRGat/1BSdBWIjChWbHH/7086cd56-c67c-4be2-a09d-06a96ebaa557.png",[1264,1266,1268,1270],{"sourceSystem":566,"sourceSystemId":1265},"7086cd56-c67c-4be2-a09d-06a96ebaa557",{"sourceSystem":566,"sourceSystemId":1267},"d29531d6-4342-446f-9bfd-68e4a35ed13c",{"sourceSystem":566,"sourceSystemId":1269},"d1493ee6-fde9-40e8-b0f6-54285ebceb75",{"sourceSystem":566,"sourceSystemId":1271},"a4027fee-4280-4b16-b0f3-2f6db85321c7",[1273],{"id":854,"text":172},{"id":854,"text":172},{"sourceSystem":937},{},[1278,1281,1285,1288,1292,1295,1299,1302,1305,1308,1312],{"id":1279,"contentType":579,"content":1280,"isHtml":13},"f6d25539-3f02-40ac-9528-e8e8eee32fce","What does it take to turn a dream into reality?\n\nFor Kachan School of Tumbling and Performance owners **Dima** and **Rebecca Kachan**, the answer is ambition, hard work and an unwavering love of sport.\n\nThe Kachan School of Tumbling and Performance, or KSTP, has grown from humble beginnings into Australia’s premier tumbling club, boasting a sensational 16 World Age, World Cup, and World Championship gold medallists. But international success was never part of the plan. In fact, when Dima and Rebecca moved to Australia in 2008, they never imagined they would one day run their own gym.\n\n“I was a former professional dancer, and Dima was a tumbler from Belarus turned circus performer,” Rebecca told Gymnastics NSW. “All we really knew how to do was perform.”\n\nAfter joining a local talent agency, Dima was invited to run an acrobatics masterclass in Windsor. There, he caught the attention a local tumbling club who invited him to their gym.\n\n“The very next week we started coaching there. Dima taught tumbling and I helped with the flexibility and conditioning.”\n\nAs they honed their skills, the couple realised that they had more to offer and soon seized the opportunity to start their own gym, founding the Kachan School of Tumbling and Performance in 2009. \n\nTheir dream? To foster the type of environment they wanted to train in when they were younger and share their love of tumbling, helping kids to learn, perform and achieve their best.",{"id":1282,"contentType":560,"content":1283,"image":1284},"eddc3df5-e5bb-4496-bae2-d93b8885f159","The KSTP team for the 2011 National Clubs Carnival.","https://media-cdn.cortextech.io/MH8SRGat/1BSdBWIjChWbHH/d29531d6-4342-446f-9bfd-68e4a35ed13c.png",{"id":1286,"contentType":579,"content":1287,"isHtml":13},"7ddd30fa-035b-4f78-bcff-24c9fa33282d","In the beginning, the club operated three days out of the Windsor District Baptist Church in South Windsor, and three days in Penrith.\n\n“We didn’t have enough equipment for two venues,\" said Rebecca. \"So we were packing trailers each week and carting equipment around between the venues.\"\n\nWhile building a business from the ground up, the couple were also raising four young children, leaving little room for downtime.",{"id":1289,"text":1290,"contentType":1018,"title":1291},"86d065c5-3f71-45a6-8210-895086f4831d","“It was a juggle, it was busy and we were working non-stop, but we loved it.”","Rebecca Kachan",{"id":1293,"contentType":579,"content":1294,"isHtml":13},"afff9608-cc65-43b9-b0eb-459c37703749","The club attended its first Australian Gymnastics Championships in 2009, with Dima becoming KSTP's first ever National Champion, taking home gold in Senior Men’s Tumbling. Unfortunately the club’s competitive aspirations were soon cut short, as Gymnastics Australia announced tumbling would be removed from the national championships due to low participation.\n\n“\\[It\\] was a devastating blow, as we had just opened a tumbling club,” said Rebecca. “All we could do was focus on not only developing our club and athletes but helping coaches and programs around Australia to do just the same thing.”\n\nOver the following years, Dima and KSTP played a vital role in rebuilding tumbling across Australia, running national training camps and fostering collaboration between coaches and clubs throughout the country.\n\n“It was a complete rebuild of the sport and working together was key. We had no financial help, no support, it was just us leading the way to hopefully inspire others and build the numbers.”\n\nTheir hard work paid off, and by 2012, tumbling was reinstated to the Australian Gymnastics Championships. Capitalising on the opportunity, KSTP has since produced an incredible 107 individual National Champions.",{"id":1296,"contentType":560,"content":1297,"image":1298},"22e0a922-cce0-4d1e-a29e-6f2e60cd02f4","Dima Kachan (back left) and KSTP representatives at the 2013 World Age Group Competition.","https://media-cdn.cortextech.io/MH8SRGat/1BSdBWIjChWbHH/d1493ee6-fde9-40e8-b0f6-54285ebceb75.png",{"id":1300,"contentType":579,"content":1301,"isHtml":13},"da6425a5-09b2-4c8d-9aa1-d46e4bc69ab2","Since celebrating its first national team selections in 2013, the club has also excelled internationally, helping to fuel Australia’s resurgence on the world stage.\n\n2025 was an especially strong year for the club, with **Breannah Cauchi** and **Ethan McGuinness** representing Australia at [The World Games](https://[hostname-redacted]/content/dazzling-debuts-and-riveting-returns-new-south-wales-impresses-at-the-world-games) and Ethan McGuinness going on to secure his [second World title](https://[hostname-redacted]/content/gold-and-silver-for-nsw-gymnasts-at-the-2025-trampoline-world-championships) at the 2025 World Championships.\n\nThe couple’s two oldest children **Timofei** and **Alexsa** **Kachan** also had a year to remember, with Timofei winning bronze on Double Mini Trampoline at the 2025 World Age Group Competition while Alexsa overcame a challenging lead up to claim a [historic double Junior World Championship title](https://[hostname-redacted]/content/sibling-success-at-2025-trampoline-junior-world-championships-and-world-age-group-competition), winning gold on both Double Mini Trampoline and Tumbling.",{"id":1303,"text":1304,"contentType":1018,"title":1291},"c557810b-17ce-4769-875e-738ccbcc34ff","“Seeing our kids representing their country would have to be unmatched as a parent. Then to sing the National anthem while they stand on the podium is next level.”",{"id":1306,"contentType":579,"content":1307,"isHtml":13},"75eae2ed-fb40-4af4-9c3a-06627b68fb79","Having grown up in the gym, 2026 will mark the first year all four Kachan children will compete in the international stream across Double Mini and Tumbling at the Australian Gymnastics Championships.\n\nWhile balancing gym life and home life can be tough, Rebecca believes it is more than worth it.\n\n“People often ask us if all our kids do this sport, which I find quite bizarre. It’s never a question for any of us,” she said. “This is our lifestyle and it’s what we work for and look forward to.”\n\nBut despite the numerous medals, trophies and titles, competitive success is not what matters most to Dima and Rebecca.\n\n“What makes us most proud of our kids is their effort and attitude towards their sport,” Rebecca said. “It’s not about the results, it’s about experience and shared opportunities.”\n\n“They push and support each other in the best way and never leave anyone behind. They work hard in all aspects of their lives, and it brings us pure joy as parents to see them reach their goals.”",{"id":1309,"contentType":560,"content":1310,"image":1311},"20e0a73a-b779-470a-b0b5-2922e3c6d7a1","The Kachan family at the 2025 Gymnastics NSW Awards.","https://media-cdn.cortextech.io/MH8SRGat/1BSdBWIjChWbHH/a4027fee-4280-4b16-b0f3-2f6db85321c7.png",{"id":1313,"contentType":579,"content":1314,"isHtml":13},"31aca409-4285-496d-801e-440b473d697e","As the club continues to grow and its South Windsor location nears capacity, KSTP is preparing for its next chapter, opening a new branch in Katoomba.\n\n“Just as in the early days at South Windsor, we hope to grow organically, continuing our good name and sharing our love of this sport with the community in the Blue Mountains.”\n\nThe club will begin running classes from the Katoomba Sports and Aquatic Centre at the start of Term 3, providing high quality coaching and proven programs and pathways to a new cohort of aspiring tumblers.\n\nFrom a shared dream to one of Australia’s most successful gymnastics clubs, KSTP’s success is a testament to passion, perseverance and community.\n\nAs the club continues to grow, one thing is certain, the KSTP story is far from finished.\n\n**The
